plan: Given my value of $10, I aim to bid below my value to ensure profit if I win. Bidding too low risks losing to rational bidders, while bidding too high risks overpaying. A bid of $5 should be competitive enough to potentially win against cautious bidders while ensuring a profit margin if successful.

Given my private value of $6, I should bid conservatively to avoid overpaying. Since the highest bidder pays the third-highest bid, I aim to win only if the third-highest bid is significantly lower than my value. I will bid slightly above a minimal value to increase my chances of winning at a favorable price, but not so high that I risk paying close to or above my value. Therefore, I will bid $1. This approach minimizes potential losses if I win and ensures any win is profitable.

Given my private value of $4, I should bid conservatively to avoid a loss. Since the bid must be in $0.1 increments and my value is relatively low, I will bid slightly above the minimum to remain competitive but not exceed my value significantly.
